outlook.statement: Focus on expanding The Byke's presence across India, with particular emphasis on metropolitan cities, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets, and both established and emerging tourist destinations. Strengthening operating capabilities, elevating guest experience, and building a scalable business model. Digital strategy focusing on social media, influencer partnerships, and revenue management system Revyog. Evaluating additional amenities and revenue streams to mitigate seasonality.

Upcoming properties in Indore (The Byke Gopur Square - 23 rooms), Nashik (The Byke Astara Club Resort - 10 Villas/30 keys + 24 Suite Apartments/48 keys), Borivali East Mumbai (The Byke Borivali East - 49 keys), Andheri East Mumbai (The Byke Sahar Airport - 59 keys)
Vision to scale up to 100 hotels and resorts nationwide; acquired 4-5 new properties that will soon be operational; several exciting projects in pipeline to expand reach and enhance offerings.

Indian hospitality sector expected to remain firm in FY2026-27 with industry revenues projected to grow 7-9% year-on-year; occupancy and average room rates continuing to improve; niche segments like spiritual journeys, destination weddings, and MICE gaining momentum

Company aims to expand footprint towards 100 hotels and resorts across the country by 2030; eight properties made operational and three new properties acquired during the year with several further projects underway

risks: Changing consumer expectations and travel patterns
Operational risks related to safety, hygiene, and service excellence
Competition from major brands expanding in mid-market category and smaller players growing through word-of-mouth and tech-enabled platforms
Unforeseen events denting demand: pandemics, geopolitical instability, natural disasters
Seasonality and cyclical nature of business with revenues typically higher in second half of financial year
Business continuity risk from accidents such as fires, natural disasters, and infrastructure failures
Geopolitical developments in West Asia and related aviation disruptions keeping fuel, logistics, and utility costs elevated
The Company is not materially exposed to commodity price / foreign exchange risk.
The Company also does not carry out any commodity or currency hedging activities.
Interest Risk: A decrease in the market yields in the government bond will increase the plan liability.

Longevity Risk: The present value of defined benefit plan liability is calculated using a discount rate which is determined by reference to the best estimate of the mortality of plan participants both during and after employment. An increase in the life expectancy of the plan participants will increase the plan's liability.

Salary Risk: The present value of defined benefit plan liability is calculated using a discount rate which is determined by reference to the future salaries of plan participants. As such, an increase in the salary of the plan participants will increase the plan's liability.

Credit Risk: The Company is exposed to credit risk from its operating activities (primarily trade receivables) and from its financing activities, including deposits with banks and financial institutions.
Liquidity Risk: The Company monitors its risk of a shortage of funds using a liquidity planning tool.
